title: Laser transit anemometry and pressure measurements inside a centrifugal compressor.
author: Rolando Antonio Corradini Neto
abstract: The aim of this end of studies project is the description and application of the Laser Transit Anemometry technique and pressure measurements technique inside a centrifugal compressor. The Laser Transit Anemometry is a non intrusive technique based on the determination of the speed of the particles immersed in the flow, which is done by two laser beams of equivalent power. For the pressure measurements campaign, a Kulite probe, series Xcq-093 car, was used. First, some aspects of the test bench are treated. The bench is located in a propulsion laboratory called LAMEP ("Laboratoire Mixte d'Energétique et Propulsion"), in Toulouse, France. The LAMEP is a facility common to SUPAERO ("Ecole Nationale Supérieure de l'Aéronautique et de l'Espace") and ONERA ("Office National d'Etudes et de Recherches Aérospatiales"). After, some characteristics of flow inside compressors are discussed. In Experimental studies chapter, the pressure and velocity measurements are discussed. About the pressure measurements, some of the topics treated are pressure captors, acquisition chain, processing data and implementation of the probes in the test bench. About the velocity measurements, some aspects of the Laser Transit Anemometry technique are treated, including the implementation of the technique in the test bench. Finally, some of the results of the experiment are discussed and a conclusion about the technique is presented.
